objective: Create the Style 9 golden concept as a dense layered-comparison poster explaining how backpressure makes production respond to actual processing capacity.

output_contract.crop_rules: preserve the full title, complete upper comparison, complete lower feedback loop including its upstream return arrow, and all three benefit cells; keep critical copy outside the outer five percent

confirmed: Without backpressure, continued production can outpace consumption, grow queued work, and increase processing delay.
With backpressure, consumer capacity and buffer-watermark state produce a feedback signal that regulates upstream production.
Memory protection, more stable latency, and lower cascading-failure risk are presented as intended benefits rather than absolute guarantees.

Represent production, buffering, consumption, and feedback as generic technical modules without vendor-specific protocols or deployment details.
